extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians, mathematical physicists, and academics debating the role of rigour vs. speculative/heuristic methods in mathematics
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria for judging the value of mathematical work, balancing formal rigour, heuristic/speculative methods, conceptual clarity, aesthetics, and interdisciplinarity. Used to evaluate contributions across pure math, mathematical physics, computational exploration, and theory-building.

rubrics_metrics.name: mathematics_as_creative_human_enterprise
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics is a creative human enterprise; rigid formalism is sterile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that mathematics is driven by human creativity and that excessive early formalization can be detrimental to discovery; values imaginative, human-centred approaches to theory-building.

rubrics_metrics.name: speculation_conjecture_and_physical_intuition
rubrics_metrics.description: Speculation, conjecture, and physical intuition are essential to mathematical progress; they should not be banished or ghettoized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage heuristic reasoning and intuition as legitimate stages of research; such work should be allowed and clearly distinguished from fully rigorous results (see honesty_about_epistemic_status).

rubrics_metrics.name: theory_organizes_past_experience
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal of theory is to organize past experience so the next generation can absorb essentials painlessly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory's role is pedagogical and synthetic: arranging concepts, examples, and techniques to make the subject teachable and accessible to students and future researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: allow_conjecture_for_growth
rubrics_metrics.description: A field that admits only fully rigorous work and rejects conjecture-driven exploration cuts off its own growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies or cultures that demand full rigour up-front can stifle new directions; permitting conjectural, exploratory work fuels development and opens avenues later made rigorous.

rubrics_metrics.name: style_elegance_vision_and_analogy
rubrics_metrics.description: A mathematician should aspire to elegance, vision, and the ability to see distant analogies, not merely to formal correctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style and vision are evaluative criteria: proofs and theories should aim for clarity, conceptual unification, and the revelation of deep analogies across subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: rigour_is_essential_but_not_sufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Rigour is essential, but rigour without ideas is pedantry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal correctness is necessary, but mathematical value also requires substantive ideas and insight; avoid valuing form over content.

rubrics_metrics.name: evolving_notion_of_rigour_and_fluency_between_heuristic_and_formal
rubrics_metrics.description: Rigour distinguishes mathematics from other sciences, but the form of rigour evolves; a good mathematician moves fluently between heuristic exploration and formal proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical standards change; what counted as rigorous in earlier eras may not now. Valued practitioners can operate at both heuristic and formal levels and know when to switch.

rubrics_metrics.name: computer_experimentation_and_visualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Computer experimentation and visualization are legitimate first-class methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical/computational exploration can produce discoveries and insights that precede proofs; treat computational results as credible contributions when appropriately documented and contextualized.

rubrics_metrics.name: conceptual_understanding_over_formal_verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Conceptual understanding is more important than formal verification; a 'theorem' understood without proof is more valuable than a proof not understood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize clarity of ideas and conceptual grasp; a formal proof that does not illuminate may be less valuable than heuristic or conceptual explanations that convey understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: continuum_between_mathematics_and_physics
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics and physics share a continuum; the boundary is not a value judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-disciplinary work (mathematical physics) should be evaluated on its own terms; predictive heuristic arguments in physics can be mathematically valuable even before formal definitions exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: physics_driven_development_and_delayed_rigour
rubrics_metrics.description: Many important late-20th-century developments came from physics and were initially rigorous only in the physical sense; demanding full rigour up-front would have prevented progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical examples (mirror symmetry, Seiberg–Witten theory) show that physics-motivated intuition can lead to rich mathematics; allow space for such developments to mature and later be formalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: appropriate_rigour_to_claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Rigour appropriate to its claim — formal proof for a formal claim; well-founded heuristic for a heuristic claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match the standard of evidence to the nature of the claim: do not require formal proof for exploratory conjectures, but require proof for formal theorems; be explicit about standards applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: honesty_about_epistemic_status
rubrics_metrics.description: Honesty about epistemic status — speculation labeled as such, theorems labeled as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should clearly indicate which statements are conjectural, which are heuristic, and which are proven; transparency about confidence and status is a criterion of good practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: generative_power
rubrics_metrics.description: Generative power — does it open new questions and tools?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate work by its ability to spawn new problems, methods, conjectures, or viewpoints; generativity is a key marker of lasting value.

rubrics_metrics.name: connection_to_other_fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Connection to other fields — utility or relevance across pure, applied, and physical domains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that builds bridges to other disciplines or integrates diverse areas is especially valuable; interdisciplinarity is a positive criterion rather than a demotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: long_term_clarification
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-term clarification — does the next generation understand the subject better because of this work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a contribution clarifies concepts and structures so future students/researchers can learn the field more readily; pedagogical impact matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: communicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicability — can the ideas be transmitted to non-specialists?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity, exposition, and the ability to convey ideas to broader audiences (students, mathematicians outside the subfield) are desirable qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: aesthetic_appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Aesthetic appeal — beauty, elegance, inevitability remain valid criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beauty and elegance are legitimate evaluative standards; a theory or proof with aesthetic virtues can be prized even before full formalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: credit_for_predictive_heuristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Predictive heuristic arguments deserve credit even when the underlying objects are not yet defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heuristic or predictive arguments that suggest fruitful mathematics should be acknowledged as valuable contributions and can justify further formal investigation.
